summary: Added the gated real-host update suite: a broken commit exits 4 with the probe reason, restarts the previous image, keeps version one serving and recorded as current; a fixed commit serves version two and records the old image as previous; a config-only env+volume update exits 0 with zero builder calls and an unchanged image set. Serialized gated integration files in vitest.config.ts because add and update share the single managed buildkitd and replaced each other's daemon when run concurrently. Typecheck, lint, 688 unit tests, the focused 4/4 suite, and the declared 10/10 integration run pass; cleanup verified.

decisions: The update fixture is a test-owned git copy of the supported Node/Express fixture with versioned response bodies, so the test controls every commit over file:// without depending on a public remote.

The broken commit is a server.js syntax error: Railpack builds the image without executing the entrypoint, so the failure is a real probe failure (exit 4) rather than a build failure (exit 3), exactly as the acceptance criterion requires.
The fixed update is a normal non-JSON CLI run so the operator-facing summary is asserted; the broken update uses --json so the exit code and structured failure details are asserted.

The config-only step changes [env] plus a newly declared volume and injects a builder that records and refuses calls, proving UPD-FR-05's no-build rule and new-volume creation; the full image set is also compared before and after as a builder-independent no-build proof.
vitest.config.ts sets fileParallelism false only when EASY_HOST_INTEGRATION=1, because the gated suites own the fixed easy-host-buildkitd name and a concurrent suite replaces it mid-build.
interfaces: tests/integration/update.test.ts consumes addApp, runUpdateCommand, UpdateDependencyOverrides, AddBuilder, createPaths, createBuildkit, Registry, containerName, volumeName, APP_LABEL/ROLE_LABEL/IMAGE_LABEL; no product interface changed.
vitest.config.ts: test.fileParallelism is disabled for gated integration runs.

warnings: The declared command's npm script already passes tests/integration, so the file argument runs every gated suite; with the new serialization all three pass together.
Observed broken-update probe reasons were 'connection closed' and 'connection reset by peer', so the suite asserts the full probe network-failure vocabulary rather than one wording.
The broken-update scenario spends the full 90s health_startup_ms in the failed candidate probe; the suite's 20-minute scenario budget carries headroom (observed 97s).
The config-only change is driven through runUpdateCommand's programmatic changes option because the CLI surface exposes only --rebuild; the real swap, probe, runtime, and config write still run.
validationLimitations: Real builds ran on x86_64 only; the cold fixture build was ~237s per run and the suite remains network-dependent for npm and Railpack/BuildKit acquisition.
A SIGKILL of the runner itself would bypass afterAll; unique names make that safe to retry, but the path is reasoned, not exercised.
npm run test:packaging cannot pass until the packaging suite is authored; it is outside UPD-1.4's scope.
payload.taskDescription: Add the gated integration test for update. Add an app from a local fixture copy, serve version one, push a syntactically broken commit, run update, and assert exit code 4, that the old container is running from the old image, that the app still answers with the version-one response, and that state still records the old image as current. Then fix the commit, run update, and assert the new version serves. Also assert a config-only update completes without a build by checking the builder was not invoked.
